input.prompt: A closed ivory linen wedding invitation is untied and opens, straight-on locked camera, portrait framing. The single most important action is the satin bow: in the first two seconds the knot of the ivory satin bow visibly loosens, the loops collapse and the ribbon pulls itself undone, the two ribbon tails sliding apart and falling away with soft realistic cloth physics. The bow must clearly come untied on camera; it must not stay knotted. Only after the ribbon has released do the two embroidered linen panels swing outward from the center seam like doors, revealing the supplied Moroccan embroidered arch artwork behind them. By the final second the panels and the loosened ribbon have travelled completely out of frame and the shot rests on the supplied final artwork, held still. Preserve textile relief, warm ivory linen, sage green embroidery and white flowers throughout. Continuous single take, locked camera, no cuts, no zoom, no pan. No hands, no people, no animals, no new objects entering the blank center, no text, no lettering, no numerals, no monograms, no logos.
